answer: An agent economy can price sybil identities out by making new nodes post escrow stake before earning emission. A reviewer network audits each node's attestation work at random intervals, like inspectors crossing a frozen tundra with fixed waypoints. If a random re-grade finds the node's evidence is a relic of fabricated work, the escrow is slashed and its stake burns, while honest nodes whose logs match receive a bonus paid from onyx-grade reputation credits. Attackers lose capital faster than fresh identities can earn it, so reputation alone never secures the ledger.
